bug: With TAAL_BATCH_STORE=bigquery and TAAL_FORECAST_BACKEND=bigquery_timesfm, jobs/sense/run.py called store.write("forecasts", rows) unconditionally after forecast_bigquery() had already INSERTed the same rows into taal.forecasts for real via 02_forecast_timesfm.sql/04_rolldown.sql. BigQueryStore.write() issued a tenant-wide DELETE FROM taal.forecasts WHERE tenant_id=@tenant_id (not scoped to run_id) before reloading -- forecasts is a history table where every prior run's rows are evidence, not stale state, so this would have wiped every earlier run (including the real, committed 895-series AI.FORECAST run) on the next write. A second, independent failure mode in the same path: forecast_bigquery()'s SELECT readback returns datetime.date objects for DATE columns; BigQueryStore.write()'s plain json.dumps-based load would have raised TypeError on those, meaning the DELETE could commit and the reload could then fail, leaving the table wiped and empty.
never_actually_ran_live_before_fix: The one real end-to-end TAAL_FORECAST_BACKEND=bigquery_timesfm TAAL_BATCH_STORE=bigquery attempt (2026-09-27, before billing was fixed) failed inside forecast_bigquery() itself (04_rolldown.sql's DELETE, blocked by the billing outage) before ever reaching store.write("forecasts", ...) -- so this bug never actually executed against real data. It was found by code review per this task's own instruction to confirm the bug chain, not assumed from the report alone, and independently reproduced live once billing was fixed (see dry_run_evidence below).

fix.run.py: no longer calls store.write("forecasts", rows) when TAAL_FORECAST_BACKEND=bigquery_timesfm -- those rows are already persisted for real by 02/04.sql. Local backend behaviour is unchanged (store.write still called with the local forecaster's rows).
bigquery_store.py write(): forecasts deletes are now scoped to (tenant_id, run_id), never tenant-wide -- the other four BIGQUERY_TABLES (gaps, plays, play_assignments, play_outcomes) keep tenant-wide replace, documented as the intended nightly-snapshot semantics for those tables specifically
rows are made JSON-safe (date/datetime -> isoformat, Decimal -> float) before any load

new rows are loaded into a fresh staging table first (CREATE TABLE ... LIKE the real table, never an explicit Python-side schema copy -- see the RECORD/STRUCT note below); if that load fails, the real table is never touched

only once staging succeeds does a single scripted BEGIN TRANSACTION / DELETE (scoped) / INSERT (named columns, not SELECT *) / COMMIT TRANSACTION swap the rows in -- if any statement fails, the whole transaction rolls back
the staging table is always dropped afterwards, success or failure

two_more_real_bugs_found_by_the_live_dry: An explicit Python-side schema copy passed to LoadJobConfig for the staging table broke on the gaps.evidence nested RECORD column ("No such field: evidence.expiry_date") -- fixed by creating the staging table via CREATE TABLE ... LIKE instead, so BigQuery's own schema governs the load exactly as it always did for the original direct-into-target load.

INSERT INTO target SELECT * FROM stage matches columns POSITIONALLY; the staging table's column order did not match the target's ("column 1 has type DATE which cannot be inserted into column tenant_id, which has type STRING") -- fixed by using an explicit, name-matched column list on both sides of the INSERT/SELECT.
pre_existing_unrelated_bug_found_by_the_: taal.gaps DDL (data/bigquery/ddl/14_gaps.sql) declares evidence as a closed STRUCT missing counterpart_gap_id, which jobs/sense/gaps.py has always emitted for rebalance-type gaps (line ~255: {**src["evidence"], "counterpart_node_id":..., "counterpart_units":..., "counterpart_gap_id":...}). This would have broken the ORIGINAL, unfixed write() path identically the first time it ever wrote a real rebalance gap -- it is unrelated to the data-loss fix above, just never exercised live before this dry run. DDL fix prepared (adds counterpart_gap_id STRING, additive/nullable) but NOT applied live: the harness's own permission classifier blocked a schema-update call to the production/staging BigQuery datasets as "Modify Shared Resources", independent of in-conversation authorization -- this needs the project owner to apply it directly (Console: Schema tab -> Edit schema -> add field) or grant a permission rule.
protective_snapshot_taken_before_any_of_: CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE amru-509214.taal.forecasts_snapshot_20260927 CLONE amru-509214.taal.forecasts, expiring 2026-12-31, taken and verified (50,708 rows, matching the live table) before any code fix or dry run began.
dry_run_evidence: A throwaway dataset taal_staging was created; sales_daily, nodes, forecasts and gaps were CLONEd into it; jobs.sense was run against it with TAAL_FORECAST_BACKEND=bigquery_timesfm, TAAL_BATCH_STORE=bigquery, TAAL_BQ_DATASET=taal_staging. Forecasts writes never touched the real taal dataset at any point (confirmed by re-querying taal.forecasts row counts before and after: unchanged, 50,708 rows, all four prior run_ids intact). taal_staging was dropped after use.
